To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Cloud-assisted BANS have to be designed and deployed according to the main characteristics of the application scenario, the type of data collected, and the processing requirements.

(i) the Cloud is a promising platform for BANs, but the current state of the art is still immature; (ii) there are many challenges to be addressed, including the need for a common data format and a common API for BANs; (iii) the Cloud can be used for BANs in a number of ways, including data storage, data processing, and BANs management.

Cloud-assisted BANS represent a promising approach to support the analysis of data generated by a network of BAN, and that the development of Cloud-assisted Body Area Networks is still in its infancy and many research challenges need to be addressed.

the development of Cloud-assisted Body Area Networks that are able to provide a scalable and efficient infrastructure for storing and processing body sensor data.
the development of a Cloud-based infrastructure for BAN data storage and processing.

the investigation of the most appropriate Cloud-based solutions to support the development of BANs, in order to provide a scalable, flexible, and efficient approach to the storage and processing of large amount of contextual sensor data streams.

the Cloud-assisted BAn paradigm is a promising research field that will enable the development of new applications for the benefit of human society.
